calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout, and misplaced focus after an invalid number.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight to 6 m.
primary_action.expected: Show the crossings affected at 6 m.
primary_action.observed: The selected 6 m control and result list show the riverside path closed, ferry stopped, and footbridge closed. Captured A-1440-before and A-1440-after.

A-1440.edge_observation: At exactly 2 m, reached with two ArrowLeft presses, the visible result lists only the riverside path closure. Captured A-1440-edge.
A-1440.fact_check: At 6 m the picture shows a moored ferry beside a FERRY CLOSED sign, with water above the bridge deck and railing visible. At 2 m it labels a submerged path, although the path itself is hard to distinguish beneath the water. The interface provides no independent source for the thresholds or real-world crossing status.
A-1440.strength: The scene connects rising water with physical landmarks, and keyboard focus is clear.
A-1440.weakness: The submerged-path label points into water where the path is difficult to identify; the scene relies on the text for that fact.
A-1440.repair: Make the path and its submerged boundary identifiable at 2 m, with a precise callout.

primary_action.input: Tab to 4 m, then ArrowRight to 6 m.
primary_action.expected: Show all three affected crossings alongside the controls.
primary_action.observed: The 6 m selection and all three result lines fit with the controls in the 390 by 844 viewport. Captured A-390-before and A-390-after.

A-390.edge_observation: At exactly 2 m, reached with two ArrowLeft presses, the screen lists only the riverside path closure. Captured A-390-edge.
A-390.fact_check: At 6 m the ferry is tethered near a small FERRY CLOSED sign and the bridge deck is under water; the railing remains visible. The submerged-bridge label overlaps part of the small scene. At 2 m the submerged-path label points into water, but the path is not readily discernible. Real-world thresholds are unsupported by a visible source.
A-390.strength: The full answer and controls remain visible without scrolling.
A-390.weakness: The small illustration and overlaid callout make the physical evidence harder to read on a phone.
A-390.repair: Reposition callouts and clarify the crossing outlines at mobile scale.

primary_action.input: Tab to 4 m, then ArrowRight to 6 m.
primary_action.expected: Show the three affected crossings at 6 m.
primary_action.observed: The 6 m selection shows the riverside path closed, ferry stopped, and footbridge closed. Captured B-1440-before and B-1440-after.

B-1440.edge_observation: At exactly 2 m, reached with two ArrowLeft presses, the result lists only the riverside path closure. Captured B-1440-edge.
B-1440.fact_check: The diagram labels each threshold and raises the water to the bridge at 6 m. The ferry is highlighted beside a landing, but there is no visible mooring or stop marker; the text supplies its stopped status. Its fixed position leaves it above the water at 2 m and below the surface at 6 m, so the diagram can obscure the physical relationship. The thresholds are not independently sourced on screen.
B-1440.strength: The cross-section and labeled thresholds make the sequence of closures easy to compare.
B-1440.weakness: The fixed ferry behaves like a threshold symbol but looks like a physical boat, creating a misleading water relationship.
B-1440.repair: Either label the diagram as schematic and use a clear stopped-service symbol, or make the boat float with the water and visibly indicate closure.

primary_action.input: Tab to 4 m, then ArrowRight to 6 m.
primary_action.expected: Show all three affected crossings alongside the controls.
primary_action.observed: The selected control and all three results fit in the 390 by 844 viewport, with the threshold diagram also visible. Captured B-390-before and B-390-after.

B-390.edge_observation: At exactly 2 m, reached with two ArrowLeft presses, the visible result lists only the riverside path closure. Captured B-390-edge.
B-390.fact_check: Threshold labels remain legible on the phone, and water reaches the bridge line at 6 m. The highlighted ferry has no explicit stopped marker and appears underwater at 6 m and above water at 2 m. The result text conveys the service state; the image alone does not. Real-world threshold claims have no visible source.
B-390.strength: Controls, answer, and labeled diagram fit together in the phone viewport.
B-390.weakness: The small ferry and its fixed vertical position make the picture's physical meaning ambiguous.
B-390.repair: Add a legible stopped-service cue and distinguish threshold markers from objects in the water.

preference.reason: B keeps the controls, complete answer, and threshold comparison readable together on the phone. Its fixed ferry creates a material visual ambiguity that should be corrected, but the labeled cross-section communicates the closure sequence more clearly overall.
